data.hypothesis: A safer hybrid may retain the throughput benefit of portable 8-byte bit-mask validation for complete blocks while avoiding fragile carried boundary state: when a block may end inside a code point, validate that block and the remaining suffix with the supplied scalar control. This tests whole-block classification and constraint masks while preserving scalar handling for boundary cases.

memory_lessons.applicability: A stateful 8-byte mask validator needs especially careful correctness checks around block boundaries; a hybrid boundary fallback is a contrasting experiment, not evidence of a speedup.
memory_lessons.claim: The previous stateful mask candidate failed protected correctness at n=1024, pattern 0; the available diagnostic does not localize the fault, and no timing was recorded.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this block-mask plus scalar-suffix variant on the official mixed-width n=65536 case and inspect boundary/truncation correctness results.

data.notes: The previous stateful mask attempt (c557b10fc09a4c93-h01) failed protected correctness, including n=1024, pattern 0; it had no timing. This candidate keeps the scalar validator as a control and tests a boundary-fallback hybrid. The bit-parallel implementation uses portable uint64_t operations rather than target-specific SIMD intrinsics; no speedup is claimed before controller measurement.
transformations: Preserved the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator as a correctness control and suffix fallback.
Used portable 64-bit word classification to validate fully contained 8-byte blocks, including continuation placement and restricted second-byte constraints.
When valid prefix masks indicate a sequence may cross a block boundary, delegated validation from that block through the end to the scalar control instead of carrying pending/range state.
Retained a scalar bounded-tail path for remaining bytes.
